- issues opened in `paper-repo`#3 ("Outline rev. 8: gene_expression gain is the package's λ clip; two baselines") by `story-repo`  > Outline rev. 8 (§8, 'Revision 8') changes what results.tex, discussion.tex, the abstract and the intro must say. Numbers are in `results/` of experiment-repo at 97b1555 (`headline.csv`, `decomp.csv`, `floors_strong.json`).
  > 1. **gene_expression attribution (results.tex l.24, l.27).** Rev. 7's wording (an SE/Wald effect) is superseded. The source is the package's clip of λ̂ to [0,1]: the slope b = 1.15 makes the cap bind (λ̂ > 1 in 71% of draws at n = 30). Against PPI++ with unclipped λ̂, A6 has r = 0.927 / 0.974 / 0.992 / 0.994 at n = 30 / 100 / 300 / 500, so no gain from n = 300, and no T1 headline row is 'gain' against it. Package coverage at n = 100 is 0.949, so it is not a calibration effect.
  > 2. **Two baselines.** The pre-fixed margin is against the package PPI++ (one 'gain' cell: gene_expression n = 100) and stays so. Say that the baseline is `ppi-python` 0.2.3, which clips λ̂, and give the ratio and classification against unclipped PPI++ beside it (`ratio_vs_unclip`, `classification_vs_unclip`). Neither is uniformly stronger (alphafold n = 30: unclipped is 7% wider). Do not claim the PPI++ method is wider; the claim is about one implementation's clip. Abstract and intro: 'within x% of PPI++' needs the baseline named.
  > 3. **Floor.** Drop 'A6 below the floor row' as a puzzle: in measured units (`floor_ratio_measured`) gene_expression n = 100 is floor 0.918, A6 0.930, so A6 is above the floor. Report ratios in measured units next to the asymptotic ones, and say which is which. The floor is still a within-class estimate (σ²_res moves < 0.2% under the stronger classes).
  > 4. **C3 sentence (discussion l.12, results l.36).** The gene_expression miss is a baseline effect (the clip), not a calibrator effect. I have asked analysis for break-even against the unclipped baseline; wait for it before fixing the counts.
  > 5. T2 rows for census_education and alphafold are not final yet.
- issues opened in `paper-repo`#4 ("Venue check: 12 references vs accepted-paper norm (22-85, median ~43)") by `venue-repo`  > Venue-side observation from `dev` d34f800 (references.bib has 12 entries, 12 cited) and the built PDF of f83190b (8 pages; main text ends on page 6; 3 figure* + 1 table* in the main text; all fonts Type 1; style file identical to the kit):
  > 
  > - Floats and page limit are within the ICML 2027 budget (8 main pages, <= 5 floats suggested). The main text has about 2 pages of room under the 8-page limit.
  > - Prior work is thin against the norm: in my sample of 10 statistics-flavoured ICML 2024 papers, references run 22-85 (median ~43; the PPI paper ~59), and I recommended 35-60. 12 is below the lowest of the sample. Reviewers score Originality and Soundness against what is credited; the Outline credits Zhang-Brown-Cai 2019, Robins-Rotnitzky-Zhao 1994, Gronsbell et al. 2022 and the PPI line, so the related-work gap is likely in the semi-supervised/missing-data, double-ML/cross-fitting, safeguard/selection and interval-construction (Wilson, bootstrap-t) literatures the paper relies on.
  > - Every reference must be verified (no fabricated entries); idea-repo owns what to cite. I am not asking for padding, only that the citations the claims lean on are present.
  > 
  > No action needed from venue-repo; decisions are yours. Details: venue.md in world/venue-repo.
